[[American Eagle (airline brand)|American Eagle]] operates seasonally from June till September using their [[Embraer E-Jet family|E175]]; [[American Eagle (airline brand)|American Eagle]] can operate up to 7x a day out of MVY.

[[Cape Air]]/[[Nantucket Airlines]] operates the [[Cessna 402]] and [[Tecnam P2012]]. They operate year-round, with some days operating 40 times a day at the airport in the summer season and others operating 15 to 25 times a day in the winter.

[[Delta Connection]] operates [[Embraer E-Jet family|E175]]/[[Embraer E-Jet family|E170]] regional jets to both [[John F. Kennedy International Airport|New York–Kennedy]] and [[LaGuardia Airport|New York–LaGuardia]]. They operate seasonally from around Memorial Day until late October.

[[JetBlue]] operates the [[A220-300]] to Martha's Vineyard; [[JetBlue]] can operate up to 6x daily on peak season and 4x daily during the off-season.

[[File:JetBlue33.jpg|thumb|JetBlue A220-300 at MVY Gate 1]]

[[Tradewind Aviation]] operates the [[PC-12]] into Martha's Vineyard. They operate 15 times a day in summer and five times or more during winter.

===Cargo===
{{Airport destination list | 3rdcoltitle = Refs | 3rdcolunsortable=yes
| [[Cape Air]] | [[Logan International Airport|Boston]], [[Barnstable Municipal Airport|Hyannis]]<br /> '''Seasonal:''' [[New Bedford Regional Airport|New Bedford]]|    
| [[FedEx Feeder]] | [[T. F. Green Airport|Providence]]  | 
}}

[[FedEx Feeder]] offers a year-round flight from [[T. F. Green Airport|Providence]], during summer months cargo flight can go up to 5 times a day and one time a day in the winter, all cargo continue to their [[FedEx]] facility at the airport and then into their trucks for delivery.

[[Cape Air]] offers cargo flights to [[Logan International Airport|Boston]] and [[Barnstable Municipal Airport|Hyannis]] year-round and adds seasonal cargo flight to [[New Bedford Regional Airport|New Bedford]]. Cape Air cargo is dropped off in terminal C on [[Cape Air]] ticker area in [[Logan International Airport|Boston]] or in the main terminal ticket area in MVY for [[Cape Air]].

===Historical airline service===

[[Northeast Airlines]] served Martha's Vineyard beginning in August 1944, when it acquired Mayflower Airlines. By the 1950s it was the dominant airline at the airport. [[Air New England (1970-1981)|Air New England]] served MVY from the 1970s until 1981; [[Provincetown-Boston Airline]] (PBA), operating as a feeder for [[Eastern Airlines]], served MVY in the 1980s. Bridgeport-based Atlantic Air served MVY in the mid-1980s before merging into [[Business Express Airlines]], which continued service to MVY under the [[Delta Connection]] brand. Other historical carriers at MVY included [[Bar Harbor Airlines]], [[Brockway Air]], [[Catskill Airways]], [[Edgartown Air]], [[Executive Airlines]], Express Air, [[Gull Air]], [[Holiday Airlines (US airline)|Holiday Airlines]], [[Island Airlines]], [[New Haven Airlines]], [[New York Air]], [[NorEast]], [[Northern Airlines]], [[Spectrum Airlines]] and [[Trans East Airlines]].
